title: Coeff_G(B(Σ), Φ)[E_Φ⁻¹] ≃ Rep_Φ(G) (§7.4 Thm)
body_html:
Localized equivalence

Let $E_\Phi$ be the class of morphisms $s$ in $\Coeff_G(\BSigma, \Phi)$ such that $H_0(s)$ is an isomorphism in $\Rep_\Phi(G)$.

Theorem (Sheaf7 §7.4). $H_0$ induces an equivalence of categories $$\Coeff_G(\BSigma, \Phi)[E_\Phi^{-1}] \;\xrightarrow{\;H_0\;}\; \Rep_\Phi(G),$$ with quasi-inverse $\Loc_\Phi$.
proof_html:
The argument is the standard localization-from-adjunction.

Adjunction. By Loc_Φ: Rep_Φ(G) → Coeff_G(B(Σ), Φ) and H_0 adjunction, $H_0$ is left adjoint to $\Loc_\Phi$, with counit $\mathrm{counit}_V : H_0(\Loc_\Phi V) \xrightarrow{\sim} V$ an isomorphism for every $V \in \Rep_\Phi(G)$ (this is the §7.1 resolution theorem Resolution theorem: C_•(Φ, V) → V (Thm 7.1.7) combined with hypothesis (S) Serre-subcategory property (S) — a consequence, not a hypothesis).

Gabriel–Zisman localization. When the counit of an adjunction $F \dashv G$ is a natural iso, the left adjoint $F$ factors through the localization $C[F^{-1}\text{-isos}]$ as an equivalence — this is [Gabriel–Zisman, Calculus of Fractions and Homotopy Theory, Prop I.1.3(ii)–(iii)]. Apply it to: - $F = H_0$, $G = \Loc_\Phi$; - $C = \Coeff_G(\BSigma, \Phi)$, $D = \Rep_\Phi(G)$; - the class $E_\Phi$ is by definition $\{s \mid H_0(s) \text{ iso}\}$.

The "counit iso" hypothesis of GZ is what we just established. The conclusion is: $$H_0 \colon \Coeff_G(\BSigma, \Phi)[E_\Phi^{-1}] \;\xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}\; \Rep_\Phi(G),$$ with $\Loc_\Phi$ as quasi-inverse on $\Rep_\Phi(G)$ (induced from the right adjoint after localization). $\square$

Remark on the unit side. The unit $\mathrm{unit}_\mathscr V \colon \mathscr V \to \Loc_\Phi(H_0(\mathscr V))$ is in general not an iso; it is an iso precisely on the cartesian subcategory $\Cosh^{\mathrm{cart}}_G(\BSigma, R, \phi) \subseteq \Coeff_G(\BSigma, \Phi)$, by the §7.2 cartesian unit-iso theorem (Cartesian cosheaves Cosh^cart_G(X,R,φ) and unit isomorphism). The localization is therefore unnecessary on the cartesian subcategory — the equivalence holds before inverting any morphisms. This is what makes the cartesian framework valuable for the §8 Res/Sat construction, where $\Res(E_\Phi) \subseteq E_M$ is checked block-by-block on cartesian cosheaves.

Example: depth-zero block (Schneider–Stuhler)

Take $M = G$, $K_x = G_x$, $K_{x,0+} = G_{x, 0+}$, $\phi_x = \mathbf 1$ on $G_{x, 0+}$. Then $\Coeff_G^0(\mathcal{B}(G))$ recovers the standard Schneider–Stuhler coefficient system category, and the localization equivalence specializes to their depth-zero result. This case is the target of the §8 reduction Main Theorem 8.2.1: Rep_Φ(G) ≃ Rep_0(M).
